metas.name: Entebbe Vibe - Entebbe - Vibe
metas.note: The city of Entebbe, southwest of Kampala, can often be recognized by feeling slightly emptier than most of the capital, with more greenery and somewhat fancier houses. The area also has significantly more street signs than the rest of the capital.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kamapla Unique Car - Kampala - Unique Car
metas.note:
This Unique Car is used everywhere throughout Kampala. It can be easily recognized by it's distinct boxy shape and squared side mirrors.

NOTE: This car can also sometimes be seen in National Parks as well as a similar one on the Island of San Andrés (east of Nicaragua), however that car has rounded mirrors.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kampala City Centre - Kampala - City Centre
metas.note: In the city centre of Kampala, you will see paved roads with black-and-white curbs. In contrast to the rest of the city, the city centre looks richer and very built-up, with lots of multi-storey buildings.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kampala Landscape - Kampala - Landscape
metas.note: Kampala is a very hilly city, and as such it is rare to get a round without elevation or noticeable hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kampala Red Soil - Kamapala - Red Soil
metas.note: Like most of the national park coverage, Kampalan soil is typically very red. Even paved roads normally have a noticeable red, purple or pink tinge.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kampala Taxi Buses - Kamapala - Taxi Buses
metas.note: Throughout Kampala, you will often see these taxi buses, with a blue blocky pattern on the sides. These are a good clue for the city if you are not able to see the Google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kibale Dark Tiny Forest Paths - Kibale - Dark Tiny Forest Paths
metas.note: The central coverage of Kibale consists of somewhat to very dark and tiny forest paths. Similar paths can be found in Semuliki, however those will be wetter and more humid.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kibale Normal Forest Roads - Kibale - Normal Forest Roads
metas.note: In the two long eastern parts of coverage in Kibale you will find yourself on forest roads that are wide enough for a car. They are also normally brighter than the central coverage and sometimes lead outside the forest.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kibale Primate Lodge - Kibale - Primate Lodge
metas.note: This easily recognizeable Lodge is located in the centre of Kibale.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kibale Tourist Information - Kibale - Tourist Information
metas.note: This building for tourist information can be found near the centre of Kibale. You can see it from three different viewing angles so remember its green color and shape.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kibale Wide Dirt Road - Kibale - Wide Dirt Road
metas.note: The coverage of the very western part of Kibale is on a very wide dirt road. This road is unique to Kibale with only few other places that may look similar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kidepo Amopuas Rock - Kidepo - Amopuas Rock
metas.note: This unique Rock can be found in the western part of Kidepo.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kidepo Apoka Safari Lodge - Kidepo - Apoka Safari Lodge
metas.note: This Lodge can be found in the northern part of the main coverage.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kidepo Hostel Bandas - Kidepo - Hostel Bandas
metas.note: These round hostels are located in the northern part of the main coverage. They can be seen from multiple angles but are sometimes hard to spot so if you're in Kidepo keep an eye out for them.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kidepo Kakine Campsite - Kidepo - Kakine Campsite
metas.note: This campsite, in the centre of the Kidepo coverage, can be easily recognized by its two circular shelters.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kidepo Katurum Lodge - Kidepo - Katurum Lodge
metas.note: This unique Lodge, surrounded by mountains and lots of vegetation, is found in the southern part of Kidepo.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kidepo Mountains and Grass - Kidepo - Mountains and Grass
metas.note: The Kidepo National Park is very recognizeable by mountain ranges being found in almost all directions. Furthermore, the grass is usually of medium length and green-golden-ish, however this might vary.
metas.footer: Image: Plonkit Note: Self researched

metas.name: Kidepo Nagusokopire Campsite - Kidepo - Nagusokopire Campsite
metas.note: Similar to the Kakine Campsite, this one also features two circular shelters, however one of them is surrounded by many trees, making them easy to tell apart. It is located in the northern part of the main coverage.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Kidepo North Forested Roads - Kidepo - North Forested Roads
metas.note: The southern half of the north road in Kidepo is somewhat forested, and as such it may occasionally be hard to see the various mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Kidepo North Wide Mountain - Kidepo - North Wide Mountain
metas.note: The northern half of the north road in Kidepo is located in a savannah and can be easily recognised by the wide mountain to the north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Lake Mburo Black Soil - Lake Mburo - Black Soil
metas.note: In a large part of Lake Mburo you can find very distinct dark and even black soil on the side of the road. You will generally only see it on the marked roads, however there are a few rare exceptions.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Lake Mburo Deciduous Forest - Lake Mburo - Deciduous Forest
metas.note: In this small part of Lake Mburo you'll be able to find yourself in a small deciduous forest. Sometimes you can also see a man in a red shirt nearby.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Lake Mburo Eagle's Nest Hotel - Lake Mburo - Eagle's Nest Hotel
metas.note: The Eagle's Nest Hotel can be easily remembered by being on top of a mountain. It can sometimes be seen from a farther away but is quite hard to spot.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Lake Mburo Lakeside - Lake Mburo - Lakeside
metas.note: You can only see the actual Lake Mburo from the road east of it, except for one other location.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Lake Mburo Tiny Village - Lake Mburo - Tiny Village
metas.note: This tiny village is the only location not east of the Lake Mburo you can see the lakeside from, making it easy to recognize.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Lake Mburo Vibes - Lake Mburo - Vibes
metas.note: Lake Mburo National Park, located west of lake Victoria, has by far the driest coverage in the country. The grass is almost always completely dried out, which is normally enough to recognise it. Bushes and trees along the road also typically look very dry. The area is quite hilly, but not mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Mount Elgon Camp - Mount Elgon - Camp
metas.note: This camp featuring two wooden benches and huts with green steel roofs is found at the western end of the eastern path.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Mount Elgon Church - Mount Elgon - Church
metas.note: This Church made of orange bricks can be found in the very west of the Mount Elgon coverage.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Mount Elgon Follow Men - Mount Elgon - Follow Men
metas.note:
On the western road of Mount Elgon you should almost always be able to see one to three men following you. Furthermore, there are two different pairs of men, one in the east and one in the west. They will be in the direction of where you should guess. (Men in the west => guess in the west)

NOTE: There are very few locations without someone or different men following you which are not covered in this map!
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Mount Elgon Top - Mount Elgon - Top
metas.note: Everywhere on top of Mount Elgon you'll be out in the open with distinct small palm-like trees. Moreover, you'll also almost always be followed by an armed man in green clothes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Airport - Murchison Falls - Airport
metas.note: This airport, easily recognized by the metal fence, is located in the western part of Murchison Falls.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Dirt Barrier - Murchison Falls - Dirt Barrier
metas.note: These dirt barriers are most commonly found in Murchison Falls National Park, however be careful as they can also be seen in other parks such as the Queen Elizabeth National Park, so use other metas to confirm your guess.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Ferry - Murchison Falls - Ferry
metas.note: This ferry, located in the centre of Muchison Falls, can be recognized by either the globe found on both riversides or by being on a platform on top of the river.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Gas Station - Murchison Falls - Gas Station
metas.note: This gas station can be found in the centre of Murchison Falls.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Grass Lines - Murchison Falls - Grass Lines
metas.note: Another, however less accurate, way to recognize Murchison Falls are grass lines running through the road, especially whenever you can't see any dirt barriers. Be careful when using this meta though since they can be found in most other parks as well.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Lodge Ruin - Murchison Falls - Lodge Ruin
metas.note: These ruins are located in the northern part of Murchison Falls.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Palms - Murchison Falls - Palms
metas.note: Seeing these palms in Uganda means you are extremely likely to be in the northern parts of Murchison Falls.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Paraa Primary School - Murchison Falls - Paraa Primary School
metas.note: This School is found in the centre of Murchison Falls.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Paraa Safari Lodge - Murchison Falls - Paraa Safari Lodge
metas.note: This Lodge is found in the centre of Murchison Falls. You might sometimes be able to recognize its entrance from farther away by the yellow curbs.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Sambiya River Lodge - Murchison Falls - Sambiya River Lodge
metas.note: The entrance to the Sambiya River Lodge is located in the more southern part of the main Murchison Falls coverage.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls Student Centre - Murchison Falls - Student Centre
metas.note: This white building is located in the centre of Murchison Falls.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Murchison Falls White Nile - Murchison Falls - White Nile
metas.note: In the western part of Murchison Falls you are often able to see the White Nile or one of its headstreams, the Victoria Nile, which is a lot smaller though.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Entale Safari Camp - Queen Elizabeth - Entale Safari Camp
metas.note: This camp features a tall, red and white metal tower which can sometimes be seen from a bit farther away.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Gas Station - Queen Elizabeth - Gas Station
metas.note: This gas station can be found on the very south western tip of the Queen Elizabeth coverage.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Grey/Brown Soil - Queen Elizabeth - Grey/Brown Soil
metas.note: Queen Elizabeth National Park is one of the only places in Uganda where you will commonly see dirt which is not red. Instead, the dirt will typically be either brown or grey(ish).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Katwe Village - Queen Elizabeth - Katwe Village
metas.note:
Katwe Village is the only large settlement besides Kampala and Entebbe. It can feature both the normal Uganda car and the national park car. If you see the Uganda car, to not mistake it with another city, look out for cacti or a large vehicle with a cage, as you're alaways able to see either one.

NOTE: The vehicle might be very far away and difficult to spot, so don't rule out Katwe if you don't spot it right away.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Kazinga Channel - Queen Elizabeth - Kazinga Channel
metas.note: If you think you're in Queen Elizabeth National Park and see a large body of water and can see the other coast nearby you should be on a road near the Kazinga Channel.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Lake Bunyampaka - Queen Elizabeth - Lake Bunyampaka
metas.note: This lake with two buildings is the only water crater that's in the very east.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Lake Edward - Queen Elizabeth - Lake Edward
metas.note: If you think you're in Queen Elizabeth National Park and see a large body of water, with the other lakeside being quite far away, you're likely along the coast of Lake Edward.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Large Cacti - Queen Elizabeth - Large Cacti
metas.note:
These large cacti can be seen almost everywhere throughout Queen Elizabeth.

NOTE: Occasionally similar cacti can be seen in other national parks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Paved Road - Queen Elizabeth - Paved Road
metas.note: This paved road is the only one outside Kampala and therefore unique to Queen Elizabeth National Park. There is also a power line running parallel to the road which can be spotted from farther away.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Queen Elizabeth Water Craters - Queen Elizabeth - Water Craters
metas.note: These large craters filled with water can be found in the north western part of Queen Elizabeth. You might not always be able to see the water, however the landscape and vegetation is easy to remember. Also, unlike other parts of this National Park you will almost never find cacti near the craters.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Semuliki Bright Paths - Semuliki - Bright Paths
metas.note: Bright forest paths, often exposed to the outside, are found on the northern half of the western coverage in Semuliki.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Semuliki Female Hot Spring - Semuliki - Female Hot Spring
metas.note: The female hot spring can be recognized by only having a sign and no shelters.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Semuliki Male Hot Spring - Semuliki - Male Hot Spring
metas.note: The male hot spring can be recognized by also featuring a sign but additionally also two shelters.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Semuliki Muddy Forest Paths - Semuliki - Muddy Forest Paths
metas.note: The southern coverage of both paths in Semuliki are usually very muddy forest paths. This is important in order to tell them apart from the ones found in Kibale which are normally dryer and covered in lots of leaves.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Semuliki South Mountains - Semuliki - South Mountains
metas.note: In a southern part of the eastern path of Semuliki you can see the distinct southern mountains. They can also be seen a bit more north but that part has very tall grass.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Semuliki Tall Grass - Semuliki - Tall Grass
metas.note: In the south of the eastern path in Semuliki there is a part outside of the forest with very tall grass. You will also almost always be able to see mountains.
metas.footer: Self researched.

metas.name: Semuliki Water Drops - Semuliki - Water Drops
metas.note: On most of the coverage in Semuliki you can find water drops on the camera lense. This is especially found in the north of the eastern path and middle of the western one.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
